key_insight: The paper shows that control, optimal transport, probabilistic inference, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and machine learning can all be viewed as optimizing free-energy-like objectives under constraints.
engineering_relevance: This unifying perspective can help engineers transfer algorithms and intuitions across reinforcement learning, variational inference, and generative modeling for more principled model design.
method: Builds a conceptual bridge across five fields using a shared variational/free-energy framework
Reviews core principles from physics and applied mathematics before connecting them to learning methods
Highlights applications in reinforcement learning, variational inference, and generative modeling
evidence_signal: The paper is a review, so its evidence is a synthesis of theory and applications rather than a new dataset or benchmark result.
watch_item: Because it is a cross-disciplinary review, practical use requires careful mapping of each theory to the assumptions and constraints of the target application.
paper_title: Bridging Control, Inference, Transport, and Thermodynamics: From Theory to Applications in Learning
